observations.text:
OBJECTIVETo assess associations of ambient UV with cardiovascular and cancer mortality across US Health Service Areas (HSAs), prioritise outcomes by signal and attributable burden, assess racial and ethnic variation, with UK Biobank corroboration.

DESIGNEcological analysis of HSAs using linear regression of crude mortality on ambient UV and social vulnerability, with correction for multiple comparisons.

SETTINGUS HSAs and UK Biobank.

DATA SOURCESPublicly available US data and UK Biobank data accessed under Application 82526.

PARTICIPANTS704 808 annual cardiovascular deaths (aged [≥]65) and 565 287 annual cancer deaths (aged [≥]50) from populations of 52.8 and 115.2 million; UK Biobank analyses included 412 665 individuals.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURESCardiovascular, all-cancer, and body-site-specific cancer mortality; regression slope per interquartile-range increase in UV ({beta} UV/IQR), modelled attributable burden for US data, and hazard ratios for the UK Biobank data.

RESULTSHigher UV was associated with lower cardiovascular ({beta}UV/IQR -68.3 deaths/100 000; P<0.001) and all-cancer mortality (-43.2; P<0.001), corresponding to 36 043 (5.1%) and 49 789 (8.8%) fewer US deaths annually, respectively. Associations varied by race and ethnicity. Cardiovascular findings were directionally consistent between US and UK datasets. All-cancer mortality and 10 of 18 cancers were inversely associated with UV in the US; UK analyses found inverse associations for all-cancer and two individual body-site-specific cancers. Twelve cancers showed directionally concordant associations across the datasets, of which ten were inverse. Lung cancer showed the strongest inverse association in each dataset.

CONCLUSIONSHigher UV was associated with lower cardiovascular and cancer mortality across US HSAs, with modelled attributable burdens exceeding 5%; UK Biobank findings provided partial corroboration. Twelve of 18 site-specific cancers were directionally concordant between datasets. US race-stratified heterogeneity did not follow a skin-colour gradient, suggesting residual confounding.

WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ON THIS TOPICAlthough intermittent ultraviolet (UV) exposure is associated with risk of increased skin-cancer incidence including keratinocyte cancers and melanoma, there is no parallel increase in mortality. In contrast, long-term ecological and cohort studies have consistently associated higher UV exposure and sun-seeking behaviour with lower all-cause, cardiovascular, and internal cancer mortality. While large-scale randomised placebo-controlled trials of vitamin D supplements have all failed their primary endpoints to reduce incidence or mortality, shifting attention toward other UV-induced pathways that may better explain the observed net benefits.

Complementary clinical evidence comes from NB-UVB phototherapy, a controlled surrogate of solar UV, which provides mechanistic insight through its association with reduced cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events and its guideline-directed role in dermatological conditions and early-stage cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

What this study addsThis study provides updated nationwide estimates of the association between long-term ambient ultraviolet radiation and mortality across US Health Service Area and UK Biobank datasets, showing inverse associations with two of the leading causes of death: cardiovascular disease and cancer. Across the observed US interquartile range of ambient UV, higher UV was associated with 36,043 fewer cardiovascular deaths and 49,789 fewer cancer deaths per year, with inverse cancer associations observed across multiple internal cancers and directionally corroborated in an independent UK Biobank dataset across all-cancer and 12 of 18 individual site-cancers.

Prespecified racial subgroup analyses showed that UV-mortality relationships were heterogeneous and non-monotonic across racial groups, rather than following the expected gradient by skin colour seen in clinical phototherapy. This suggests that UV-mortality associations may be shaped by additional biological, behavioural, environmental, or social determinants not fully captured by the Social Vulnerability Index.
observations.title: Cardiovascular and cancer mortality inversely associated with long-term ambient ultraviolet exposure across US Health Service Areas with UK Biobank corroboration

observations.text: Brugada syndrome (BrS) is an inherited arrhythmia disorder with limited drug therapy, quinidine being the principal agent. Loss-of-function variants in SCN5A reduce the cardiac sodium current (INa), but the arrhythmogenic imbalance also depends on the transient outward potassium current (Ito). Here we generated human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardioids with right-ventricular identity from a patient carrying an SCN5A frameshift variant (p.A665Gfs*16) and characterised them by patch-clamp and optical mapping. BrS cardioids showed 60% lower peak INa, more than doubled Ito, 38% slower conduction and 76% longer spontaneous cycle length. We then tested AR-788, a benzylaminothiazole- benzimidazole carboxamide of the ARumenamide class. In wild-type (WT) cardiomyocytes AR-788 inhibited Ito concentration-dependently (12%, 30% and 42% at 5, 10 and 20 {micro}M; extrapolated IC50 25.4 {micro}M), and at 10 {micro}M it returned BrS Ito to the level of untreated WT cells (21.71 vs 21.48 pA/pF, p = 0.9716) without reducing INa. It also reduced the rapid delayed-rectifier current (IKr) tail current by 40%, a liability requiring formal proarrhythmia profiling. These data identify AR-788 as an Ito-suppressing member of the ARumenamide class and provide proof of concept that a small molecule can correct the potassium-current excess in a human BrS model.
observations.title: The ARumenamide AR-788 suppresses the transient outward current in human iPSC-derived right-ventricular Brugada cardioids

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

observations.title: Effect of Atf7 knockdown via RNA interference on gene expression during MGT-reprogramming of primary murine neonatal cardiac fibroblasts

observations.text:
ObjectivesMachine learning models for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) are rarely evaluated externally or for calibration. We developed explainable models for grade II-IV acute and moderate-to-severe chronic GVHD and evaluated their transportability across multiple cohorts.

Materials and methodsGradient boosting models were trained on three CIBMTR registry-derived datasets (N = 2,509) and externally evaluated in six cohorts (N = 14,788), including a Middle Eastern cohort. We assessed discrimination (AUROC), calibration (logistic recalibration intercept and slope; Brier score), and SHAP feature explanations.

ResultsInternal discrimination was higher for chronic (AUROC 0.736) than acute GVHD (0.624); chronic calibration was good (intercept +0.258, slope 1.073), whereas the acute model was underdispersed (slope 1.802). Externally, the chronic model retained modest, above-chance discrimination (AUROC 0.54-0.64), whereas acute performance fell toward chance (0.52-0.57). Calibration drifted unpredictably, overestimating risk in 9 of 10 evaluable cohort-outcome combinations (intercepts -0.78 to +0.15; slopes 0.12 to 1.98; Brier 0.23-0.27).

DiscussionRoutine registry variables carry a transportable signal for chronic GVHD, but acute GVHD likely requires additional biological or clinical predictors. Neither the direction nor the magnitude of calibration drift could be anticipated from training performance.

ConclusionInternal performance does not guarantee external utility. Cohort-specific recalibration and routine calibration reporting are required before any clinical use; this study offers a reusable template for multi-cohort external evaluation of clinical prediction models.

Lay SummaryAfter a stem cell transplant from a donor, the donors immune cells can attack the patients body, a complication called graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). It can appear early (acute) or months later (chronic), and knowing who is at highest risk before transplant could help doctors plan prevention and follow-up. We built computer models that estimate GVHD risk using information routinely recorded at transplant, trained them on 2,509 patients from a large US transplant registry, and then tested them on six other groups totalling almost 15,000 patients, including patients from the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. The model for chronic GVHD kept a modest ability to separate higher-from lower-risk patients in every group, but the model for acute GVHD performed little better than chance outside the data it was built on. In almost every new group, both models overestimated how many patients would develop GVHD, by amounts that could not be predicted in advance. This shows that a model that works well where it was developed may not work elsewhere, and that its risk estimates must be checked and adjusted locally before it is ever used to guide care.
observations.title: External Evaluation and Calibration Drift of Explainable Machine Learning Models for Acute and Chronic GVHD Prediction After Allogeneic HSCT

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

metadata.summary: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) exhibit limited efficacy against lung cancer brain metastases, often resulting in rapid and inevitable resistance. However, the unique mechanisms driving this brain microenvironment-specific therapeutic failure remain elusive. Here, utilizing in vivo orthotopic models and single-cell RNA sequencing, we reveal that targeted therapy induces a distinct, metabolically hyperactive senescent cell subpopulation that drives rapid EGFR-TKI tolerance in brain metastasis. We identify the molecular chaperone CRYAB as an indispensable driver specifically upregulated within this senescent persister state. Mechanistically, CRYAB physically interacts with VDAC2 at the outer mitochondrial membrane, promoting endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria tethering and calcium influx. This CRYAB-VDAC2 axis orchestrates adaptive mitochondrial fission, hyperactivating oxidative metabolism while simultaneously shielding（preventing？） senescent cells from fatal oxidative stress. Genetic or pharmacological blockade of mitochondrial fission completely abolishes CRYAB-mediated therapeutic resistance. Therapeutically, we demonstrate that a 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) dietary intervention acts as a potent in vivo senolytic strategy, directly dismantling the CRYAB-dependent resistance network, eradicating senescent persister cells, and synergistically prolonging overall survival when combined with Osi. Furthermore, high baseline CRYAB expression in pre-treatment primary lung biopsies clinically predicts lower intracranial objective response rates and shorter progression-free survival in a cohort of advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients. Collectively, our study uncovers a novel CRYAB-VDAC2-mitochondrial fission axis that enforces therapy-induced senescence and highlights 25HC dietary intervention as a highly translatable combinatorial strategy to overcome EGFR-TKI resistance in brain metastasis.

observations.title: CRYAB-driven mitochondrial fission induces senescence to promote adaptive resistance to EGFR-TKI in LUAD brain metastasis

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.title: Spatial genome and transcriptome co-mapping reveals clonal heterogeneity in tumor tissue [RNA-Seq]

observations.text:
BackgroundConcurrent wasting and stunting (WaSt) is a severe form of child undernutrition, linked to higher mortality and long-term negative health outcomes. Malnutrition is a significant challenge in Yemen, where the country is experiencing a long-standing conflict, food insecurity, and socioeconomic deprivation. But there is still limited evidence on the burden and determinants of WaSt in Yemen on a national level. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and identify factors associated with WaSt among children under 5 years in Yemen.

MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional analysis using nationally representative data from the 2022-2023 Yemen Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS). A significantly large dataset of 17,734 children aged 0-59 months from all the 22 governorates of Yemen was analyzed. Concurrent wasting and stunting (WaSt) were defined as the coexistence of a weight-for-height z-score (WHZ) below -2 standard deviations and a height-for-age z-score (HAZ) below -2 standard deviations from the WHO Child Growth Standards in the same child. Survey-weighted logistic regression was performed to analyze the factors associated with WaSt among the under 5 children in Yemen.

ResultsThe national prevalence of WaSt was 8.4% (95% CI: 7.6-9.2). The highest prevalence of WaSt was found in children aged 12-23 months (12.0%) and in the Western Coastal region (11.6%). After adjustment, male sex (AOR 1.52, 95% CI: 1.30-1.80), residence in the Western Coastal (AOR 2.00, 95% CI: 1.60-2.40), Eastern (AOR 2.00, 95% CI: 1.50-2.70), and Southern regions (AOR 1.60, 95% CI: 1.20-2.10), poorest household wealth (AOR 1.96, 95% CI: 1.30-2.90), moderate (AOR 1.51, 95% CI: 1.13-1.94) and severe food insecurity (AOR 1.94, 95% CI: 1.40-2.60), and recent diarrhoea (AOR 1.22, 95% CI: 1.02-1.44) were associated with higher odds of WaSt. Having a handwashing facility and improved sanitation were protective.

ConclusionAt least 1 in every 12 under-five children in Yemen was affected by WaSt, and there were significant socioeconomic, geographic, food-security and WASH-related factors influencing this devastating outcome. Instead of simple, one-dimensional approaches, multi-sectoral interventions are needed to address this adversity. And those efforts must be integrated into the system, interconnected with each other and specifically targeted to vulnerable children and households.
observations.title: National Prevalence and Determinants of Concurrent Wasting and Stunting among Under-Five Children in Yemen: Evidence from the 2022-2023 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey

observations.text:
BackgroundPassively collected smartphone and wearable data, combined with genomic information, may enable scalable early identification of youth who are at risk for substance use disorder. However, heterogeneous data collected in naturalistic settings limit researcher control over data quality, requiring substantial preprocessing. Data cleaning and feature engineering decisions can meaningfully influence analytic outcomes yet are often minimally described or omitted in published work.

ObjectivesWe provide rationales and recommendations for common preprocessing challenges in passive sensing research, including establishing inclusion criteria when "outliers" may reflect true behavioral variability, analyzing differences across smartphone operating systems, handling observations collected outside protocol windows, and engineering features for machine learning applications.

MethodsWe illustrate principled approaches to these challenges using smartphone and Fitbit data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive DevelopmentSM Study (ABCD). The sample was drawn from the available half of the year-4 follow-up (data release 5.1; N = 4,754; ages 13-14).

ResultsExtreme outlying observations were concentrated among low-engagement participants with few observed days. Smartphone usage among Apple users appeared under-recorded relative to Android users when compared with self-report measures. Fitbit-derived behavior differed systematically between observations collected within versus outside protocol windows. We also identified potential errors in the studys default preprocessing pipeline.

ConclusionWe recommend prioritizing person-level inclusion criteria that preserve meaningful behavioral variability, examining temporal distributions rather than assuming observations are exchangeable, and thoroughly investigating and reporting data quality issues. Although illustrated using the ABCD Study, these principles broadly apply to research using smartphones, wearables, and other digital data sources.
observations.title: Sense and Sensibility: Sensible Quality Control and Data Decision-Making in Passive Sensing Data for Adolescent Substance Use Risk Prediction

metadata.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. Despite upregulation of TGFB1, the rest of the canonical TGF-β pathway was consistently downregulated in MFS, indicating a potential compromise of TGF-β signaling and lack of stimulus for SMC differentiation.

observations.title: Single-cell Analysis of Aneurysmal Aortic Tissue in Patients With Marfan Syndrome Reveals Dysfunctional TGF-β Signaling

metadata.summary: Background: Direct reprogramming of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into induced cardiomyocytes (iCMs) holds promise as a therapeutic strategy for heart regeneration. Post-myocardial infarction (MI), resident quiescent CFs (QCFs) activate and differentiate into myofibroblasts (MFs) in the infarcted region that drive pathological cardiac fibrosis. Converting these injury-activated MFs into iCMs could simultaneously alleviate fibrosis and replenish lost cardiomyocytes. However, whether the marked heterogeneity of CFs in the infarcted heart—and in particular the activation of QCFs into MFs—creates an intrinsic barrier that limits the reprogramming of these injury-activated MFs remains unknown. Methods: To define the molecular basis of this heterogeneity, we purified PDGFRα⁺ cardiac fibroblasts and used Postn lineage tracing to distinguish injury-activated MFs from quiescent CFs, enabling matched comparison of their reprogramming competence and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiling of post-MI CF subpopulations. A targeted in vitro shRNA screen was conducted against 9 MF-enriched TFs as candidate molecular barriers for cardiac reprogramming. The lead candidate was validated in mouse MFs, QCFs, human iPSC-derived MFs, primary human cardiac fibroblasts, and in vivo using dual-recombinase-mediated lineage tracing. Mechanistic insights were gained through integrated bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq and Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), together with functional assays including DNA-binding–deficient and domain-swap MEOX1 mutants. Results: We identified the upregulated transcription factor MEOX1—a known fibrosis determinant downstream of the key post-MI cytokines TGF-β1 and IL-1β—as the principal molecular barrier responsible for the profound reprogramming resistance of MFs. MEOX1 knockdown markedly enhanced reprogramming efficiency in both mouse and human MFs and enabled GATA4-free reprogramming combinations. This inhibition depended on MEOX1’s transcriptional activation activity, as disrupting its DNA-binding domain or fusing it to a repressor domain rescued reprogramming. Integrated scRNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses revealed that MEOX1 binds and stabilizes a fibrotic, MF-defining transcriptional program that antagonizes the cardiogenic program, while also modulating the inflammatory response; its knockdown disrupted this fibrotic network to favor iCM fate acquisition. Using stringent dual-recombinase lineage tracing, we demonstrated that MEOX1 knockdown enables highly efficient in vivo MF-to-iCM conversion, leading to significant reductions in cardiac fibrosis and substantial improvement in cardiac function after MI. Conclusions: Our study identifies the pathological upregulation of MEOX1 as a key mechanism underlying the reprogramming resistance of post-MI MFs, in both mouse and human. Overcoming this barrier achieves unprecedented, lineage-confirmed in vivo reprogramming efficiency, thereby addressing a significant obstacle for the clinical translation of in situ reprogramming therapies. Data included in this Series comprise the original bulk RNA-seq datasets of MGTM-reprogrammed mouse cardiac fibroblasts with control or Meox1 knockdown and with control vector/GFP or MEOX1 overexpression; RNA-seq datasets from human iPSCs, iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived myofibroblasts; scRNA-seq datasets from MGTM-induced iCM cultures and normal or day-3 post-MI mouse hearts; MEOX1 CUT&Tag data; and the newly added three-biological-replicate bulk RNA-seq dataset comparing MGTM + shCtrl with MGTM + shMeox1 used for the revised manuscript.

observations.title: Overcoming Intrinsic Barriers in Myofibroblasts Permits Efficient Cardiac Reprogramming Post-Infarction

observations.text: Bimanual actions are common in daily life, yet how task demands shape reliance on learning and control mechanisms remains largely unknown. We examined this in 73 participants who lifted a plate in virtual reality while we distorted visual motion of their right hand. During right-hand-only lifting, aftereffects were present but incomplete. Bimanual lifting with the same right-hand perturbation shifted learning further from adaptation toward feedback control: participants developed compensatory hand adjustments and showed smaller aftereffects. Relaxing precision demands improved success but neither restored aftereffects nor reduced compensation. Removing interlimb conflict by perturbing both hands did not improve success but eased compensatory adjustments and restored plate aftereffects to unimanual levels. Success rate during learning did not correlate with aftereffects, but faster movement speed did. This demonstrates that precision demands and interlimb conflict independently shift learning strategy in bimanual contexts.
observations.title: Task demands shift motor learning from adaptation to feedback control in an unconstrained bimanual task

metadata.summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/− mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II–treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/− mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility–HFpEF interactions.

observations.text: Early detection of individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P) improves access to preventive care. We developed and internally validated the E-DetectioN Tool for Emerging mental disoRders (ENTER), a multimodal digital screener designed to improve community identification of CHR-P compared with an established approach (PQ-16 cut-off). Participants aged 12-35 years from the UK and Italy completed the online ENTER screener, assessing attenuated psychotic symptoms, processing speed and environmental risk factors. Participants above the PQ-16 cut-off and a random subset below were assessed with the Comprehensive Assessment of At Risk Mental States (CAARMS). PQ-16 cut-off and ENTER models were developed using (penalised) logistic regression, random forest and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) within a repeated nested cross-validation framework with semi-supervised learning incorporating unlabelled data. Models were evaluated by discrimination, calibration and clinical utility. 2,522 participants completed the ENTER screener. 495 underwent CAARMS assessments. 124 (25.1%) met CHR-P criteria; 2,027 participants were not assessed with the CAARMS (unlabelled). ENTER showed improved discrimination (C=0.744, 95%CI: 0.697-0.790) compared to the PQ-16 cut-off (C=0.625, 95%CI: 0.570-0.682, p=0.003) and similar calibration (ENTER: slope=1.02, 95%CI: 0.78-1.32; PQ-16 cut-off: slope=0.39, 95%CI: 0.19-0.52, p=0.074). At a clinically relevant threshold, ENTER identified approximately 2 additional CHR-P individuals per 100 assessments compared with the PQ-16 cut-off. Compared with established PQ-16 cut-off pre-screening, ENTER showed higher performance for community identification of CHR-P individuals. Multimodal digital screening might support more informative community triage before specialist assessment. External validation and implementation studies are required to establish real-world clinical utility.
observations.title: Refining E-detectioN Tools for Emerging mental disoRders (ENTER) to identify young people at clinical high risk for psychosis in the community: model development and internal validation

observations.text: Learning to read leads to widespread changes in brain organization, but it is not yet known when text first becomes a privileged stimulus. To test whether neural sensitivity to text can appear prior to reading instruction, 31 monolingual toddlers in Israel (2.1-3.6 years) not yet enrolled in school were presented with displays of real, native text and visually matched non-text symbols. Using functional near-infrared spectroscopy, we found different patterns of activity in response to text vs. non-text across multiple cortical regions. Most notably, text elicited more activity in the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, a region often associated with language processing. These results suggest that through implicit sensitivity to regularities in their input, toddlers may be able to discover that text is a meaningful stimulus and could begin to develop associations that will allow them to build connections between language and text.

metadata.summary: Tumor heterogeneity arises from the sequential acquisition of somatic mutations and the selection of fitter clones, leading to distinct genotypes and phenotypes. Joint mapping of genome and transcriptome in the same tumor tissue can directly link clonoal relation to transcriptional state enabling a more in-depth understanding of intrinsic and extrinct tumor heterogeneity in the tissue context. Here, we introduce Spatial-GT-seq, a spatial multi-omic technology capable of genome-wide co-profiling of the genome and transcriptome at near single-cell resolution. We demonstrated in situ identification of tumor subclones in a mouse model of lung metastasis, with parallel transcriptomic profiles indicating that the gene expression profile of the same tumor clone is altered by the tumor microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis of primary and recurrent human pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors reveals both persistent and newly emerging tumor subclones, exhibiting transcriptional changes in both the original and recurrence sites. These findings highlight Spatial-GT-seq as a valuable platform for studying genotype-phenotype-microenvironment associations, providing new insights into cancer evolution and heterogeneity.

observations.text: Ocean warming and marine heatwaves threaten seagrasses, which are considered highly vulnerable to rising temperatures. We compared thermal stress responses of the tropical seagrass Halophila stipulacea collected from the Gulf of Aqaba in 2017 and 2022. Under mesocosm-applied thermal stress, 2017 plants showed reduced growth, impaired photochemistry, and extensive transcriptomic changes. In contrast, 2022 plants maintained normal growth and photochemistry with minimal transcriptional responses. The enhanced thermal stress tolerance of 2022 plants was associated with a 'stress-ready' transcriptome, with many stress-response genes already up/downregulated under control conditions, including those encoding heat, oxidative stress, and abscisic acid signaling proteins. These changes coincided with local ocean warming and a shift from episodic to chronic thermal stress. Our findings provide the first longitudinal dataset in a seagrass that tracks physiological and molecular changes occurring concurrently with documented ocean warming.

observations.text:
BackgroundSocial vulnerability is associated with adverse health outcomes, but existing social vulnerability indices often rely on cohort-based and self-reported data, potentially limiting their population-level applicability. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an SVI from routinely collected electronic health records (EHRs) using natural language processing (NLP) and examine its association with mortality and healthcare utilization.

MethodEHR data from 193,629 individuals aged 35-102 from the Wellbeing Services County of Central Finland between years 2010 and 2023 were used in this study. A 6-item SVI (total score 0-6) was developed from free-text clinical notes using deep-learning-based NLP. SVI scores were calculated at baseline and annually for individuals. Associations between baseline SVI and all-cause mortality and healthcare utilization were assessed over 12-year follow-up using Cox and count models.

ResultsThe mean baseline SVI among all participants was 0.35 (range 0-6). Women had higher SVI (0.39) than men (0.32, p<0.001). SVI increased with age. One unit increase in SVI was associated with a higher risk of mortality (Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.23; 95% Confidence Interval (CI) (1.21-1.24), a higher odds of using healthcare services (Odds Ratio (OR) = 1.20; 95% CI): 1.19-1.21) and a greater healthcare service use (Incidence Rate Ratio (IRR) = 1.07; 95% CI: 1.06-1.07).

DiscussionAn index capturing multiple domains of social vulnerability can be derived from EHRs using NLP. Higher SVI was associated with increased mortality and healthcare utilization. These findings support the potential of EHR data for assessing social vulnerability and related health risks.

metadata.summary: Heart failure (HF) is a growing global health crisis with a persistently poor prognosis, increasingly recognized as an inflammatory disease driven by CD4+ T lymphocytes that promote cardiac fibrosis and stiffness. Current therapies fail to address this immune component effectively. Here, we introduce first-in-class, drug-free Nano-Immuno-Metabolic Modulators (NIMMs) that ameliorate fibrosis by systemically reprogramming macrophage metabolism to curb pro-fibrotic T cell responses. Through high-throughput screening, we identified a lead candidate, NIMM22, which accumulates in the spleen and lymph nodes and potently upregulates macrophage arginase-1 expression. This metabolic shift depletes local L-arginine, suppressing CD4+ T cell effector function and their subsequent recruitment to the heart. NIMM22 treatment alleviated fibrosis and restored cardiac function across multiple murine cardiomyopathy models, including hypertensive and genetic disease. Chronic administration revealed no systemic toxicity or broad immune suppression, a safety profile confirmed in non-human primates. Our work establishes a new paradigm for cargo-free nanotherapeutics that modulate the cardiosplenic axis, offering a targeted, immunotherapy-like strategy with broad potential for treating cardiac and other immune-mediated fibrotic diseases.

metadata.summary: Background: Hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) may extend donor heart preservation beyond conventional storage durations. We evaluated early graft function and myocardial cellular and metabolic integrity following porcine heart transplantation after 20 hours of HOPE.  Methods: Ten donor hearts underwent various preservation conditions: static cold storage (SCS) for 4 hours (n=2), HOPE for 4 hours (n=3), and HOPE for 20 hours (n=5), followed by heart transplantation (HT) in recipient pigs. Following implant and reperfusion, graft function was assessed over 3 hours by serial echocardiography, invasive hemodynamics, optical flow analysis, and vasoactive support scoring; myocardial tissue was analyzed by histopathology, flow cytometry, mitochondrial respirometry, transcriptomics, and proteomics.  Results: Ejection fraction, right atrial pressure and systolic blood pressure did not differ significantly between groups, and no graft met criteria for primary graft dysfunction. LV contractility was within normal range with comparable vasoactive support among all groups. Preservation-associated weight gain was greatest after HOPE 20h, and histopathology showed comparable findings with edema present in all cohorts, without fibrosis, thrombosis, or necrosis. Cardiomyocyte viability was preserved across all groups (HOPE 20h, 86%, HOPE 4h, 81%, and SCS 4h, 77%). Maximal oxygen consumption rate was elevated in HOPE 20h versus HOPE 4h and SCS 4h (p<0.01), while basal and non-mitochondrial respiration were similar. Transcriptomics and proteomics revealed minimal differences in gene and pathway expression among groups.   Conclusions: HOPE preserves donor heart viability, mitochondrial integrity, and ventricular function after 20 hours of ischemia in a porcine model, without evidence of primary graft dysfunction, supporting extended preservation for heart transplantation. Edema, recovery of function, and metabolic responses warrant further investigation with longer-term monitoring.

metadata.summary: Developing arteries must withstand pulsatile blood flow while remaining sufficiently flexible to accommodate changing hemodynamic demands. Endothelial interactions with perivascular cells and extracellular matrix are essential for this balance, but the signaling mechanisms that coordinate them remain incompletely understood. We previously showed that SH2 domain protein E (She), an endothelial adaptor protein implicated in ABL signaling, limits the size of the dorsal aorta (DA) in zebrafish embryos. Here, we investigated why zebrafish she mutants subsequently develop DA collapse and circulatory failure at 4–5 days post-fertilization. Before circulatory failure, the mutant DA retained an approximately circular cross-section and showed no detectable changes in the endothelial cell geometry, but exhibited increased distensibility during the cardiac cycle. Mutants had fewer perivascular stromal cells between the DA and posterior cardinal vein, smaller perivascular col1a1 and col5a1 expression domains, and reduced col1a1 transcript level. Single-cell RNA sequencing independently identified a reduced relative abundance of perivascular fibroblast subpopulation. In contrast, DA-associated mural cell numbers, laminin immunoreactivity, and local col4a1 transcript levels were not detectably altered. Ablation of pdgfrb-positive cells largely prevented DA narrowing and circulatory failure, while the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside provided partial rescue. These findings support a contribution of mural cell-dependent vascular tone to collapse of the mechanically vulnerable DA. Mutants also exhibited cardiac chamber enlargement, increased atrial and bulbus arteriosus deformation, atrioventricular regurgitation, and increased Elastin B accumulation in the enlarged bulbus arteriosus. However, endocardial-specific She expression failed to rescue circulatory failure, supporting its requirement in vascular endothelium. Together, these findings link She function to perivascular fibroblast abundance, fibrillar collagen-gene expression, and arterial stability. They support a model in which impaired perivascular support renders the developing DA susceptible to mural cell-associated collapse, extending the role of She from early vessel-size regulation to maintenance of vascular function.
